subject.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content

question: Should upgrades invalidate pre-fix unpromoted recall state, add a narrowly identifiable QMD repair through memory-core doctor, or explicitly accept a tested bounded age-out period?
rationale: The store lacks reliable backend provenance, so parsing every persisted diff-looking snippet could corrupt legitimate content, while silently retaining the rows leaves existing users partially broken; the acceptable upgrade tradeoff requires feature-owner intent.

options.title: Invalidate old recall state
options.body: Version or mark the recall cache and rebuild unpromoted rows after upgrade, avoiding ambiguous parsing of persisted content.

options.title: Add doctor repair
options.body: Expose a conservative memory-core doctor repair that removes or reconstructs only confidently identified contaminated rows.

options.title: Accept bounded age-out
options.body: Document and test the exact duration or refresh events after which contaminated rows can no longer affect Dreaming.

recommendation.title: Invalidate old recall state
recommendation.body: Version or mark the recall cache and rebuild unpromoted rows after upgrade, avoiding ambiguous parsing of persisted content.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the upgrade contract for the short-term recall and promotion system introduced in their feature-history work.
